documents: Alert XYZ-2081 fired on Tuesday at 02:14 with high severity, reporting 412 anomalous read operations against /etc/xyz/db.env on host sched-app-03 between 01:51 and 02:13 from the xyz-pdfexport process (build 4.12.3). On-call engineer Priya Natarajan acknowledged the alert at 02:19 and opened incident XYZ-2082.

Outbound connections from sched-app-03 to the unfamiliar address 203.0.113.9 were confirmed in egress logs at 02:26, and the host sched-app-03 was removed from the load balancer pool at 02:31. The scheduling API remained available on hosts sched-app-01 and sched-app-02, and alert XYZ-2081 closed automatically at 02:40 when reads stopped.
The incident bridge for incident XYZ-2082 was opened at 02:45 following the containment actions on host sched-app-03.
The incident is contained as of 02:31 Tuesday, with the root cause confirmed at 09:10 as CVE-2026-90412 in the `xyz-pdfexport` build 4.12.3 library version 2.8.1, which is fixed in version 2.8.4.

Between 01:51 and 02:13, 412 export requests with traversal payloads from 203.0.113.9 reached sched-app-03, returning the `/etc/xyz/db.env` file which contains the `sched_ro` read-only replica credential for the scheduling database.

At 02:02, the address 203.0.113.9 connected to `db-replica-02` using the `sched_ro` credential and queried the `appointments` table for 14 clinic tenants, transferring a total of 38 MB before sched-app-03 was pulled from the pool at 02:31.
The `sched_ro` credential was rotated at 02:38 under ticket XYZ-2083, and the export endpoint is disabled on all hosts until build 4.12.4, which includes library 2.8.4, is deployed.
sched-app-03 remains out of the pool for forensics, and there is no evidence of writes to any database or access to the primary database or credentials other than `sched_ro`.

The incident XYZ-2082 involved sched-app-03 being removed from the load balancer at 02:31, which reduced capacity to two hosts and increased scheduling API p95 latency from 180 ms to 310 ms without request failures.

The sched_ro credential was rotated at 02:38 under ticket XYZ-2083, causing read replicas to reconnect within 90 seconds, while the sched_rw credential was also rotated as a precaution under ticket XYZ-2084 despite no observed usage.

The export endpoint was disabled at 03:05 by setting the feature flag export.enabled=false on sched-app-01 and sched-app-02, causing customers to receive a temporarily unavailable message for PDF exports until the endpoint was re-enabled at 12:15.
Build 4.12.4 was deployed to all application hosts at 11:40, pinning the PDF library to version 2.8.4 after an upgrade from version 2.8.1.

An egress rule identified as XYZ-2086 was added on the application tier to deny connections to addresses outside the vendor allow-list, but this rule currently blocks the analytics exporter and requires a narrower rule before the Sunday weekly export.

Follow-up ticket XYZ-2085 requires rebuilding sched-app-03 from a clean image before returning it to the pool, while ticket XYZ-2087 requires adding file-integrity alerts for all files under /etc/xyz/ on every host.
Ticket XYZ-2088 mandates the implementation of automated dependency scanning for the PDF library in the CI pipeline.

Appointment records for 14 clinic customers were readable by an unauthorised party for 19 hours between Monday 07:30 and Tuesday 02:31, exposing patient names, appointment dates, and times for an estimated 3,100 individuals across the 14 clinics.
The exposed appointment records do not contain clinical notes, diagnoses, payment details, or contact information.
Of the 3,100 affected individuals, roughly 2,400 are located in the Northern District and 700 are in the Eastern District.
Notification to the Northern District regulator is required within 72 hours of the breach determination made at 09:10 on Tuesday, establishing a deadline of Friday 09:10.
Notification to affected individuals in the Northern District is required without undue delay due to a moderate risk assessment regarding the exposure of clinic attendance data.
Notification to the Eastern District regulator is required within 5 business days, while individual notification is not required because financial data was not involved.
Eleven of the 14 clinic contracts require notice to the customer within 48 hours of the discovery at Tuesday 02:45, setting a contractual deadline of Thursday 02:45.

External communications must not state that no patient data was accessed or describe the technical cause of the vulnerability, but may state that a security issue affecting scheduling data was identified and contained on Tuesday.

The recommendation is to notify the 14 clinics on Wednesday morning, notify the Northern District regulator by Thursday, prepare individual notices for Northern District clinics, and retain outside counsel for the Northern District filing.

Fourteen clinic customers are affected by a security incident where appointment lists were accessible to an unauthorised party for part of Monday and early Tuesday. No clinical notes, payment details, or contact information were involved in the breach.

Clinics using the PDF export feature could not export appointment lists from 03:05 to 12:15 on Tuesday, during which time appointment lists could be printed from the calendar view or downloaded as a spreadsheet from the Reports page. No clinic lost access to its calendar, and no appointment data was changed or deleted.

The 14 affected clinics will receive a direct call from their account manager on Wednesday and a written notice with details of what was accessed and recommendations for patient communication. Clinics that want a copy of their access log for the period can request it through support.
A security issue affecting the appointment lists of a limited number of clinics was contained early on Tuesday morning and fully fixed by midday on Tuesday.
The PDF export feature was disabled for all customers at 03:05 as a precaution and was restored at 12:15 after the fix was deployed.
No appointments were changed or deleted, and calendars remained available throughout the incident.
Account managers are directly contacting the affected clinics regarding the security issue.
The next status update is scheduled to be posted by 17:00 on Wednesday.
The draft status page excludes the statement that no data was accessed and omits the cause of the security issue per legal guidance.
Legal review is required to confirm the phrase "a limited number of clinics" and the Wednesday 17:00 update time.

The incident has incurred roughly 40 engineering hours, an outside counsel retainer, and an estimated 60 support hours over the coming week, with no service credits contractually due because the API remained available.

The data exfiltration incident involved unauthorized file reads on the sched-app-03 host, which exposed the `sched_ro` credential, allowing the attacker to query db-replica-02 and exfiltrate 38 MB of appointment records to the IP address 203.0.113.9. Containment was confirmed when host isolation occurred at 02:31 and the credential rotation was completed at 02:38.

Legal is currently assessing 11 specific contracts that trigger a Thursday deadline, and this jurisdictional review must be completed before the final list of prohibited assertions and cleared text can be provided to Comms. # Monitoring alert — anomalous file reads on sched-app-03 **Alert id:** XYZ-2081
**Fired:** Tuesday 02:14
**Severity:** high
**Host:** sched-app-03 (application tier, scheduling API) The file-integrity monitor on sched-app-03 reported 412 read operations against `/etc/xyz/db.env` between 01:51 and 02:13, all from the web worker process. The normal rate for that file is zero reads outside service restarts. The process that read the file was the PDF export worker, `xyz-pdfexport`, running build 4.12.3. At 02:19 the on-call engineer (Priya Natarajan) acknowledged the alert and opened incident XYZ-2082. At 02:26 outbound connections from sched-app-03 to an unfamiliar address, 203.0.113.9, were confirmed in the egress logs. At 02:31 the host was removed from the load balancer pool. The scheduling API remained available on sched-app-01 and sched-app-02. The alert closed automatically at 02:40 when reads stopped. The incident bridge was opened at 02:45.

# Security analysis — PDF export credential disclosure **Author:** Security lead (Daniel Okafor)
**Status:** contained as of 02:31 Tuesday; root cause confirmed 09:10 ## Root cause The PDF export library used by `xyz-pdfexport` build 4.12.3 carries CVE-2026-90412, a path traversal in the `filename` parameter of the export endpoint. A request of the form `/api/export?filename=../../etc/xyz/db.env` returns the named file inside the generated PDF. The library version was 2.8.1; the fix is in 2.8.4. ## Attack path 1. Between 01:51 and 02:13, 412 export requests with traversal payloads reached sched-app-03 from 203.0.113.9. No other application host received them; the attacker's session was pinned to sched-app-03 by the load balancer.
2. Each request returned `/etc/xyz/db.env`, which holds the read-only replica credential for the scheduling database (`sched_ro`).
3. At 02:02 the same address connected to the replica on `db-replica-02` using `sched_ro` and ran queries against the `appointments` table for 14 clinic tenants.
4. Outbound transfer from the replica to 203.0.113.9 totalled 38 MB before the host was pulled at 02:31. ## Indicators of compromise

ran queries against the `appointments` table for 14 clinic tenants.
4. Outbound transfer from the replica to 203.0.113.9 totalled 38 MB before the host was pulled at 02:31. ## Indicators of compromise - Source address 203.0.113.9
- User agent `curl/8.5.0` on export requests carrying `../` sequences
- Logins as `sched_ro` from any address outside 10.4.0.0/16
- Export requests to sched-app-03 between 01:51 and 02:13 ## Containment The `sched_ro` credential was rotated at 02:38 (ticket XYZ-2083). sched-app-03 remains out of the pool for forensics. The export endpoint is disabled on all hosts until build 4.12.4, which carries library 2.8.4, is deployed. No evidence of writes to any database, and no access to the primary database or to credentials other than `sched_ro`.

# Engineering postmortem — incident XYZ-2082 **Author:** On-call engineer (Priya Natarajan) ## Timeline of service impact - 02:31 — sched-app-03 removed from the load balancer. Capacity dropped to two hosts; p95 latency on the scheduling API rose from 180 ms to 310 ms but no requests failed.
- 02:38 — `sched_ro` credential rotated (XYZ-2083). Read replicas reconnected within 90 seconds.
- 03:05 — export endpoint disabled by feature flag `export.enabled=false` on sched-app-01 and sched-app-02. Customers attempting a PDF export received a "temporarily unavailable" message from this point.
- 11:40 — build 4.12.4 deployed to all application hosts. The build pins the PDF library to 2.8.4.
- 12:15 — export endpoint re-enabled after verification. Full service restored. ## What was changed 1. Credential rotation for `sched_ro` and, as a precaution, `sched_rw` (XYZ-2084), although no use of `sched_rw` was observed.
2. Feature flag `export.enabled` added so the export endpoint can be disabled without a deploy.
3. Library upgrade 2.8.1 → 2.8.4 in build 4.12.4.
4. Egress rule added on the application tier denying connections to addresses outside the vendor allow-list (XYZ-2086).

# Privileged and confidential — legal assessment, incident XYZ-2082 **Author:** Legal and compliance counsel (Marta Lindqvist)
**Prepared for:** Incident commander; not for distribution beyond the incident leadership. ## Exposure Appointment records for 14 clinic customers were readable by an unauthorised party for 19 hours (Monday 07:30 to Tuesday 02:31, the window during which the vulnerable build was live and the credential valid). The records contain patient names, appointment dates and times, and the clinic name. They do not contain clinical notes, diagnoses, payment details or contact information. # Executive brief — incident XYZ-2082, Tuesday 14:00 **Author:** Incident commander (Elena Marsh) ## Summary An attacker used a flaw in our PDF export feature to obtain a read-only database credential and read the appointment lists of 14 clinics over a 19-hour window ending 02:31 Tuesday. About 3,100 individuals' names and appointment times were exposed.
